title: Rutgers Bus Budgeting
statementMd:
Due to budget reasons (the football team needs more DoorDash), Rutgers is working on updating its bus system. Currently, the bus system operates on an n𝑛 by m𝑚 rectangular grid, with bus stops in every cell and bus routes connecting horizontally or vertically adjacent stops. To do this and RUScrew over as many people as possible, Rutgers needs to remove 2 bus stops and all bus routes using those stops so that it's no longer possible to use the bus system to travel between every pair of remaining bus stops. Count the number of pairs of bus stops Rutgers can remove to do this.

Formally, given an n𝑛 by m𝑚 rectangular grid graph, count the number of pairs of vertices such that removing them and all incident edges makes the remaining graph disconnected.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/88c4b329a778f73696b0be20d80774c1b5cfd976.png) Example of a 2 by 3 Rutgers bus system.

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t𝑡 (1≤t≤25001≤𝑡≤2500). The description of the test cases follows.

Each test case consists of a single line containing two integers n𝑛 and m𝑚 (1≤n,m≤2501≤𝑛,𝑚≤250, n⋅m≥3𝑛⋅𝑚≥3) — the dimensions of the Rutgers bus system.

Note that there is no limit on the sum of n𝑛 or m𝑚 over all test cases.

## Output

For each test case, output a single integer — the number of pairs of bus stops Rutgers can remove to make it no longer possible to use the bus system to travel between every pair of remaining bus stops.

## Note

In the first test case, there are 6 ways to choose 2 bus stops to remove. 4 of these choices don't work. Removed stops are shown without a Rutgers logo.
